concepts.name: Bonsai aesthetic styling judgment (selecting/applying named styles to evoke age)
concepts.open_problem: No formal model captures the non-deterministic aesthetic judgment by which a stylist chooses among canonical styles and bends the rules to evoke an 'air of age'; styles guide but do not determine the design, so the creative decision stays tacit.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - styling for wabi-sabi/age aesthetics is a fine-art judgment; no factory process makes aesthetic styling decisions on a living tree
concepts.app_market_check: 'bonsai styling app' - AI image generators (Bonsai Empire 'AI generated Bonsai') produce concept pictures, but no app makes the real-tree aesthetic styling decision; rate very-low
concepts.verbatim_quote: The various accepted styles will guide a bonsai designer, but are not completely deterministic.

concepts.name: Watering bonsai 'by feel' (reading moisture from pot weight, soil feel/smell, foliage look)
concepts.open_problem: Experts judge when to water from pot weight, soil feel and smell, and foliage appearance rather than a fixed schedule; this multi-sensory intuitive judgment is acknowledged to exceed what the eyes (or a sensor) can capture and resists codification.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - industrial/greenhouse irrigation uses soil-moisture sensors and automated drip, but those automate a setpoint, not the holistic by-feel judgment for an individual styled tree
concepts.app_market_check: 'bonsai watering app' - SATURATED: Bonsai Care App, Bonsai Buddy, Greg all give species/climate watering reminders; they schedule, but do not replicate the tactile/olfactory judgment; rate low
concepts.verbatim_quote: A bonsai expert with 25 years of experience emphasizes that there is more to be learned about soil by feel and smell that your eyes will ever give you.

concepts.name: Bonsai wiring (gauge selection and bending choreography to reposition branches)
concepts.open_problem: A professional judges by eye how far a branch must move and picks wire gauge, anchor and coil angle accordingly, timing removal before the wire scars growing bark; success is decided at a prep stage that is half engineering, half choreography and largely unautomated.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - no industrial wire-forming process trains a living branch over months while judging bark scarring; it is a hands-on craft skill
concepts.app_market_check: 'bonsai wiring app' - essentially none; tutorials/videos exist but no app or machine performs species-aware branch wiring; rate very-low
concepts.verbatim_quote: Professionals will take one look at a branch and think by how much it needs to be moved before choosing the correct size.

concepts.name: Deadwood techniques (jin/shari/uro carving to mimic natural weathering)
concepts.open_problem: Carving stripped trunk/branch wood to convincingly mimic lightning, drought or breakage damage so each piece looks naturally weathered and 'tells a story' is an open aesthetic-craft problem with no generative or robotic capability.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - decorative weathering of standing live deadwood for art has no factory analog (industrial wood weathering/distressing works on harvested lumber, not a living styled tree)
concepts.app_market_check: 'bonsai deadwood carving app' - none found; only how-to articles and a Wikipedia page; rate none
concepts.verbatim_quote: These techniques mimic natural deadwood formation caused by lightning, drought, or branch breakage in the wild.

concepts.name: Penjing landscape composition (shumu/shanshui/shuihan: shaping trees, rocks, water as 3D poetry)
concepts.open_problem: Composing a miniature landscape that 'captures the spirit of nature' by jointly shaping trees, selecting/placing rocks and water is a holistic artistic composition problem; no system plans or executes such multi-element living compositions.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - artistic miniature-landscape composition ('three-dimensional poetry') has no industrial production analog
concepts.app_market_check: 'penjing design app' - none found beyond inspiration galleries; rate none
concepts.verbatim_quote: They are often referred to as living sculptures or as three-dimensional poetry, and their artistic composition captures the spirit of nature and distinguishes them from ordinary potted plants.

concepts.name: Hedgelaying pleacher cut (cutting/bending stems near-horizontal while leaving them alive)
concepts.open_problem: The craftsman must partially cut and bend each stem without breaking it, leaving just enough bark and sapwood to keep the pleacher alive; how much to leave is explicitly described as a tacit part of 'the art' that varies by stem and species.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - no factory process partially severs and lays living stems into a stock-proof living fence; mechanical hedge cutters only trim
concepts.app_market_check: 'hedge laying app' - none found; only courses, guides and competition pages; rate none
concepts.verbatim_quote: A section of bark and some sapwood must be left connecting a pleacher to its roots to keep the pleacher alive - knowing how much is one part of the art of hedgelaying.

concepts.name: Hedgelaying regional-style execution and competitive judging (Midland, Devon, Yorkshire, etc.)
concepts.open_problem: ~35 regional styles each demand different angles, spacing, binders and tools, and judges weigh stock-proofness, regrowth quantity/quality, traditional style, wildlife value and appearance simultaneously - a multi-objective tacit evaluation with no computational model.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - regional craft-style aesthetics and multi-criteria competitive judging have no industrial analog
concepts.app_market_check: 'hedgelaying style app' / 'hedge competition judging app' - none found; rate none
concepts.verbatim_quote: The judges were looking for a combination of stock-proofness, the quantity and quality of re-growth, traditional style, wildlife value and overall appearance.

concepts.name: Topiary / espalier shaping of living plants into defined forms over years
concepts.open_problem: Training and clipping a living plant into a clearly defined geometric or fanciful 'living sculpture' (or flat espalier form) over years requires anticipating growth and making cut decisions that maintain form as the plant changes - partly tacit and only narrowly automated.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - this is the ONE shaping task with a real research/industrial-style analog: the EU TrimBot2020 vision-guided robot autonomously trims boxwood topiary and rose bushes to an ideal shape
concepts.app_market_check: 'topiary trimming robot/app' - TrimBot2020 research robot exists (stereo-camera + arm) and commercial robot mowers trim hedges, but no general autonomous artistic topiary/espalier shaper; rate low
concepts.verbatim_quote: The robot navigates over varying terrain and approaches rose bushes and boxwood topiary, to trim them to an ideal shape.

notes: v2 hypothesis largely SUPPORTED for the aesthetic-shaping judgment. Strongest white space (no-industrial-analog AND zero/near-zero AI): bonsai deadwood jin/shari carving, penjing landscape composition, hedgelaying pleacher cut, and hedgelaying regional-style + competitive judging - all tagged has_industrial_analog=no with ai_penetration none, and NO dedicated app/machine found. Bonsai wiring and aesthetic styling judgment are also no-analog with only very-low AI (AI image generators make pictures, not real-tree decisions). The CLEAR EXCEPTIONS to the hypothesis: (1) bonsai WATERING is app-saturated (Bonsai Care App, Bonsai Buddy, Greg) and has a partial industrial analog (greenhouse moisture-sensor/drip irrigation) - but apps only schedule, they do not replicate the by-feel/by-smell judgment experts describe; (2) TOPIARY/ESPALIER shaping is the one task with a genuine partial industrial/robotic analog (EU TrimBot2020 vision-guided boxwood/rose trimming robot) and low AI penetration. HONEST caveat: bonsai/plant apps DO exist and are numerous, but they cluster on care-scheduling/ID; the AESTHETIC and structural-shaping judgment (styling, wiring, deadwood, penjing composition, the live-stem pleacher cut, regional hedge styles) remains essentially untouched by AI and lacks any factory process. Verbatim quotes were taken from WebSearch result snippets; direct Wikipedia WebFetch returned HTTP 403, so Wikipedia-attributed quotes reflect the snippet text actually seen, not a re-fetch of the page.
